question.leadin: During this rebellion, a Muslim group called the Hansu Braves set fire to Hanlin Academy during the Siege of the Foreign Legations.
question.text: Name this rebellion which occurred during the Qing [Ching] dynasty and was defeated by the Eight-Nation Alliance.
question.answerHtml: Boxer Rebellion [or Boxer Uprising; or other synonyms for “rebellion;” or Yihetuan Movement]
question.clue: In this conflict the Seymour Expedition was defeated with the help of the Muslim Kansu Braves.

swap.leadin: In his pseudo-historical book 1421, Gavin Menzies claimed that an explorer from this dynasty visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus.
swap.text: Name this Chinese dynasty, renowned for its blue and white porcelain, which succeeded the Yuan dynasty and preceded the Qing dynasty.
swap.clue: Its first emperor came to power during the Red Turban Rebellion and was known as Zhu Yuanzhang, the Hongwu Emperor.

question.text: The construction of over six thousand backyard steel furnaces was a part of this economic policy by which Mao planned for China to modernize in a short period of time.
question.answerHtml: Great Leap Forward [also accept Second Five-Year Plan or Dayuejin]
question.clue: This period grew out of a conference in the resort city of Qingdao and the Anti-Rightist Campaign.

swap.text: The Chinese Civil War resumed after World War II, and in 1949, Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists were forced to retreat to this island.
swap.clue: The Treaty of Shimonoseki gave Japan control of this island in 1895, and the Allies at the 1943 Cairo Conference elected to return this island to Nationalist China.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about Japanese expansion before the attack on Pearl Harbor.
question.text: The first major fighting of the war occurred in the assault on this coastal Chinese city. Peter Harmsen described this battle as the "Stalingrad of the Yangtze" because of its immense casualties.
question.clue: The Oyama Incident prompted reinforcements for the existing garrison in this city of three German-trained infantry divisions.

swap.leadin: A system of law enforcement called baojia(BAO-jee-ah) was implemented during this dynasty by Wang Anshi (wong AN-shee).
swap.text: Name this Chinese dynasty that invented gunpowder, which initially helped it fight off a Mongol invasion before it was replaced with the Yuan (YOO-un) Dynasty.
swap.clue: Bi Sheng worked under this dynasty, which switched lines of succession due to the Jingkang Incident.

question.text: The kingdom of Wei was founded by this man's son, Pi. This warlord won the Battle of Guandu, and served as the chancellor to the last Han emperor.
question.clue: This man originally rose to power as a Chancellor of the Eastern Han dynasty in its waning days.

swap.text: This man was the first president of the Republic of China, and lived in Japan during his exile.
swap.clue: His party's ideals were expressed in works like the Five-Yuan Constitution and the Three Principles of the People.

question.text: The anecdote about the Bai Qi (bye chee), "The Human Butcher," appears in this text by Sima Qian (suh-mah chee-EN), which claims that the Xia (sh'YAH) Dynasty were the first rulers in the lands that comprise modern-day China.
question.clue: This text describes the melting of thousands of enemy weapons to create twelve colossal metal statues, a loyalty test in which a man points to a deer and calls it a horse, and the "rectification of weights and measures."

swap.text: It occurred between December 1937 and March 1938. Adults, children, and infants were slaughtered and massive atrocities by soldiers occurred. Many Japanese textbooks still omit any mention of it. For 15 points-give the common name for this mass killing that occurred in a major Chinese city.
swap.clue: One infamous incident during this event was the "kill one hundred people with a sword contest" that was "won" by Toshaki Mukai.

question.leadin: The yin privilege allowed high ranking bureaucrats to place their sons into low positions of power without having to deal with this system.
question.text: Name this system, success in which allowed scholar-bureaucrats to advance by demonstrating knowledge of wenxue. The challenging Eight-legged essay was an integral part of this system.
question.answerHtml: Chinese imperial examinations [accept equivalents like the Chinese civil service exams]

swap.text: This city in Shaanxi province was formerly a capital of China called Chang'an. It is home to the Wild Goose Pagoda as well as Qin Shi Huang Di's terra cotta army.
swap.clue: The Silk Road had its eastern origin in this city, where Emperor Qin Shi Huangdi was buried with his Terracotta Army.

question.leadin: This state gained power thanks to Shang Yang's reforms, and the kingdom of Han instantly surrendered to this kingdom when King An believed they would invade.
question.text: Name this kingdom whose leader Ying Zheng conquered six other states, which began a namesake dynasty.
question.clue: Li Si advised this dynasty's most notable ruler, who eventually died due to mercury poisoning while trying to find the elixir of life.

swap.leadin: The Cheng Wu manuscript describes a dream of this dynasty's queen Tai Si foretelling their victory over their predecessors.
swap.text: Name this dynasty established after its predecessors were defeated at the Battle of Muye. The Five Classics, including the I Ching, are traditionally thought to have been written during this dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Zhōu (“joe”) dynasty [or Zhōu Cháo; accept Eastern Zhōu or Western Zhōu or Xīzhōu or Dōngzhōu]
swap.clue: A "Second" dynasty of this name ruled from Shendu until its founder, Wu Zetian, abdicated.

question.leadin: Answer the following about royals who were assassinated by Serbian nationalists.
question.text: The coup in which Alexander I was killed is named for this month. This month also names a series of anti-Semitic laws passed by Alexander III of Russia.
question.clue: The New York chapter of the Prairie Fire Organizing Committee was the basis for a "Communist Organization" formed by members of the Weather Underground, named for the 19th of this month.

swap.leadin: Some of these people became idolized by the peasantry after they moved to the countryside and founded seowon ("SUH-wun").
swap.text: Name this class of people who staffed the Hall of Worthies. A "forest" of these people formed the Sarim faction before they were purged by the Hungu.
swap.answerHtml: scholars [or seonbi; or literati; or academics; prompt on officials or bureaucrats or ministers or civil servants]
swap.clue: The intensive preparation needed to become one of these people by undertaking the Gwageo meant most were also a yangban.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a Chinese province.
question.text: The Xiang River runs through this Chinese province whose name means "south of the lake" due to its proximity to Lake Dongting. Mao Zedong established a short-lived namesake soviet here in 1927 after the Autumn Harvest Uprising.

swap.leadin: Name these people associated with the Manchu reign of China.
swap.text: The Manchus took Beijing from this rebel who had seized the city from the last Ming emperor and proclaimed himself the first emperor of the Shun dynasty.

question.leadin: In a battle named for this location, Charles Elliot ordered British ships to fire on Chinese junks enforcing a food sale embargo that had been triggered by a deadly bar fight, thus beginning the First Opium War.
question.text: Identify this location that is often said to include a namesake peninsula. The 14K ("fourteen-K") organization enjoyed near-autonomy in a neighborhood named for this location that was demolished in the 1990s.
question.answerHtml: Kowloon [or Gáulùhng or Jǐulóng; accept Kowloon Peninsula or Kowloon Walled City]

swap.text: Peaceful "wo lei fei" in Hong Kong often participate in protests by performing this action. A controversial law passed in June 2020 made it a crime to lodge "insults" when this action was taking place in Hong Kong.
swap.answerHtml: singing [accept answers like singing the official or unofficial national anthem; accept playing a national anthem]
swap.clue: The Baltic countries gained independence from the Soviet Union in a "revolution" named for this action. That revolution named for this action included the formation of a human chain across all three countries.
